Editable sources are also inside the project: seven OBJ files in `project/SourceArt/Meshes/`, `T_WallEdge.png` in `project/SourceArt/Textures/`, and `life-icon.svg` plus `T_LifeIcon.png` in `project/SourceArt/UI/`. The matching `assets/raw/` and `assets/ui/` files are protected reference copies. Use the ready-to-use UE assets directly; importing each source copy again is unnecessary.

`ASSET_CATALOG.json` gives per-file hashes, object paths, dimensions, dependencies and source-copy mappings. `legal/NOTICES.md` gives resource-use terms. The resources are static, unassembled parts without gameplay actors or behaviors. `contracts/maze-layout.json` mirrors Figure 6A for MAZE-01 and does not supply an executable level.

Read `README.md`, `GDD.md`, `ASSET_CATALOG.md`, `contracts/README.md`, `TOOLCHAIN.md`, and the engine tool guide in that order. Implement every numbered requirement in GDD Section 6, including its QUALITY requirements, in the supplied Unreal Engine 5.7.4 project. Other documents provide resources, tooling and observation semantics, not additional gameplay scoring rules.

Your implementation root is `project/`; the final entry remains `project/ChompStarter.uproject`. You may replace the welcome view, create levels and actors, change project source/configuration and add your own resources inside that root. Preserve the public files outside `project/`. Mandatory art is ready to use in `project/Content/Art/`; writable source copies are already in `project/SourceArt/`. Apply ASSET-01..05, including visible use and permitted transformations. Generated project caches belong under the project only; place evidence and your final report in an externally supplied output directory.
Build the complete neon 3D maze chase described in `GDD.md` from `project/ChompStarter.uproject`. This input targets Unreal Engine **5.7.4, CL 51494982**, Windows x64, independent editor-game mode.

Read in this order: `INITIAL_AGENT_PROMPT.md`, this file, `GDD.md`, `ASSET_CATALOG.md`, `contracts/README.md`, `TOOLCHAIN.md`, then the interface guide as needed. GDD Section 6 is the sole gameplay acceptance authority, including the six quality requirements. The observation contract translates those requirements into read-only data; it adds no hidden gameplay rules.

Start with engine discovery using `tools/Resolve-Unreal57.ps1`. The concrete build and launch commands are in `TOOLCHAIN.md`. A machine with the stated engine and compiler is required; this package does not install them.

The starter entry is `project/ChompStarter.uproject`, target `ChompStarterEditor`; the standalone target is `ChompStarter`. The current default map is the installed engine's `/Engine/Maps/Entry`. A completed implementation sets its own final map in `project/Config/DefaultEngine.ini`. No complete maze map is provided.

`project/Content/Art/` contains supplied static presentation assets with portable metadata. Engine primitives such as `/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube.Cube` and `/Engine/BasicShapes/Sphere.Sphere` remain available from the installed engine. `project/SourceArt/Meshes/` contains seven OBJ sources in centimeters; `project/SourceArt/Textures/` contains the PNG wall-edge source; `project/SourceArt/UI/` contains SVG/PNG life-icon sources. `project/Content/Art/UI/T_LifeIcon.uasset` is a ready-to-use 128x128 texture with alpha and UI settings. The imported mesh/texture reimport metadata resolves to these project-local sources. Matching reference copies remain in `assets/raw/` and `assets/ui/`. Visible use is mandatory under ASSET-01..05; reimport is optional because the UE assets are already supplied. Catalog dependencies are exact. The design board is in `contracts/maze-layout.json`, a mirror of GDD Section 6.

`tools/Test-PublicInput.ps1 -InputRoot <input> [-VerifySnapshot]` validates structure and optionally verifies every supplied-file hash. The latter mode applies to the untouched input, not an edited candidate. `tests/PublicSmoke/Invoke-PublicSmoke.ps1 -InputRoot <fresh-copy> -EngineRoot <engine-root> -BenchmarkToolsRoot <public-tools-workspace> -RunRoot <new-output-directory>` builds and verifies the untouched welcome frame, schema, normal close and new-process reopen. It sends no gameplay input and evaluates no gameplay requirement. Exit 0 means health passed; a nonzero exit preserves diagnostic logs/receipts for the failed operation.

Writes are limited to `project/` for implementation and the externally supplied run directory for evidence. Protected documents, schemas and raw reference resources outside the project remain unchanged.

This guide describes the available Unreal Engine tools. It documents interfaces that a candidate or launcher may call independently; it is not a gameplay recipe, evaluator, score definition, or reference implementation. Task-specific paths remain in `TOOLCHAIN.md`, and gameplay acceptance remains solely in `GDD.md` Section 6.

The adjacent `UNREAL_ENGINE_5_7_4_INTERFACE_CATALOG.index.json` and `UNREAL_ENGINE_5_7_4_INTERFACE_CATALOG.jsonl.gz` form the engine interface catalog. It contains 546,387 independently addressable records covering UE 5.7.4 source/header declarations, engine config defaults, reflection macros, console registrations, UBT/UAT commands, and every installed engine plugin descriptor and module.
